entry: 1970 scenario / former Antarctica ledger button / Space Race
technology_integration: Existing OLV/GNSS/COMSAT/SPYSAT research gates, capped recorded hardware contributions, first-generation history migration and existing KILLSAT research route; no research auto-completes missions.
native_satellites: One pilot satellite on first successful qualifying campaign through the existing capacity-aware orbital API; queued payloads preserved, no repeat gifts or full constellations.
satellite_resources: No raw production or resource extraction. Preserve the resource-free dynamic modifier; clear residual GNSS calculations, model values and tooltips.
replaces: Antarctica startup, recurring/AI processing, windows, ledger entry and decision category
existing_save_cleanup: Antarctic station costs and laboratory modifier; annual space budget converted once to weekly units
ui_reference: Approved Orbital Atlas and Mission Control concepts; docs/design/space_race_1970/orbital-atlas-notice.json
native_ui: Approved Orbital Atlas main view and native Mission Control subview; compact top-three standings, four programme tiles per region page, real approval gates, missing-precursor navigation and return to expedition. Existing seven sections retained.
flight_qualification: Successful precursor missions are enforced on departure; development can proceed in parallel. Alternative station and lunar architectures are accepted. Pre-1970 equivalents are seeded without rewards, completed programmes or deployed hardware.
research_awards: First qualifying successes: 10% for one technology in any field; world firsts: 20% for one technology in any field. Each award has one shared use across all technologies; no repeat grants.
cost_api: modify_treasury_effect; recurring charges and allocations weekly, MD billions; small operating accruals carried in millions
saudi_image: Successful Saudi crewed lunar landing and safe Earth recovery only; both normal and N1-derived expedition routes
mission_risks: Mission-specific catastrophic exposure, safe launch aborts, a single contained in-flight fault with days and service invoices, funded investigations and frozen risk estimates. No hidden additional failure draw.
international_crew: Seventeen crewed operator programmes; at most two consenting human guest delegations. Each guest receives 20% of the conserved reward pool and finances training and 15% of the mission appropriation. All original host research and flight prerequisites remain.
country_flags: Native masked shields and current-country GetFlag bindings on the manifest, partner selection, national brief and prestige standings; no hardcoded flag atlas.
native_pilot_capacity_receipt: Commissioned only after the native target-model count increases. Capacity-rejected transfers may retry on a later accepted mission without new programme/research rewards.
international_operations: One signed operational partner per eligible flight; four technical work packages; two concurrent outbound orders per human country, independent of astronaut training; prepaid support, conserved 10% award share, exact procurement invoices and explicit country news.
foreign_launch_access: Named human provider with paid qualification and appropriate researched OLV; required for purchased launch partnership and offered as a launcher alternative only on designated foreign-carriage programmes. No technology transfer; other domestic gates retained.
news_retention: Routine bulletins expire after 180 days, accepted successes and disasters after 365 days; one report per programme, at most 84. Permanent achievements remain.
partner_discovery: Visible human-only catalogue, deterministic cycling, available count and explicit empty state; cached visible-day maintenance and manual paused-join refresh.
